arms.better: tm found the relevant append in completions.go and produced the right capacity-limiting fix, but it spent substantial context repeating reads/searches and never submitted the ticket: the first attempt hit the 64-step limit, the retry ended without submission, and retries were automatically scheduled. A user would have seen ‘Run tm run T-1 again to retry’ and then the same failure again, without a clear checkpoint or clear assurance that the underlying edit was complete. The bare `tm events` invocation also returned usage/help text (‘The durable event log: tail, inspect, replay, and verify the hash chain’) instead of directly showing useful event history. Preserve a run transcript automatically, identify repeated investigation, and make failure/retry state and next steps explicit. The hidden test passed against the retained source edit, but tm itself did not claim ticket completion.

OpenCode quickly located the append in completions.go, made a narrowly scoped copy-before-append change, ran `go test ./...` and `git diff --check`, and accurately described the fix. It could improve by adding a regression test of its own or explicitly reproducing the reported `os.Args` behavior before editing; the regression test was subsequently overlaid from the merge commit for the independent mechanical verification, which passed.
